children: Coal inventories at power plants stood at around six days of consumption as of 10 October, against a normative requirement of 19 to 20 days, while domestic production declined 3.2 per cent year-on-year

Coal stocks at India’s power plants stood at around six days of consumption as of 10 October, well below the normative requirement of 19 to 20 days, prompting concerns over the sector’s ability to meet a sharp increase in electricity demand, even as rating agency ICRA raised its FY27 demand growth forecast to 8.5 per cent from 6.5 per cent earlier.

Icra said in a note that any further decline in inventories, particularly if accompanied by weaker domestic production or supply constraints, could limit power plants’ ability to meet peak demand. The agency said a sustained recovery in coal production and supply would be important to rebuild adequate buffer stocks.

Domestic coal production declined 3.2 per cent year-on-year during the first five months of FY27, largely due to lower output from Coal India. Coal supplies to the power sector, however, increased 4 per cent during the same period.

Despite higher supplies to power plants, coal inventories remained below the levels recorded over the previous three years. Stocks of around six days were also substantially below the normative requirement of 19 to 20 days, leaving a narrower buffer against disruptions.
Average spot power tariffs on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) stood at Rs 7.7 per unit as of 10 October, compared with Rs 7.3 per unit in September and Rs 2.6 per unit in October 2025.
Although prices moderated from September amid adequate supply availability, particularly during solar hours, they remained higher than a year earlier as electricity demand stayed firm.

Icra said power tariffs during FY27 would depend on the evolving balance between demand and supply, as well as the pace of capacity additions. The agency highlighted the importance of a sustained recovery in coal production and supply to maintain adequate inventories as electricity demand grows.
